LASG ANNOUNCES TRAFFIC ADVISORY, DIVERSION PLAN FOR AJEGUNLE CITY YOUTH MARATHON

The Lagos State Government has announced a traffic diversion plan ahead of the Ajegunle City Youth Marathon, organised by the Society for Information and Human Advancement. The event is scheduled to hold on Saturday, 13th December, from 6:00 a.m.

To ensure the safety of participants and seamless traffic management, partial road closures will be implemented along the following routes:

Maracana Stadium, Ojoku Street, Baale Road, Kirikiri Road, Wilmer Link Bridge, Okito Street, Kopariwo Street, Mba/Cardoso Street, Baale Road (Secretariat), Cemetery Street, Ojora Street, Baale Aiyetoro Street, Olowojeunjeje Street, Oduduwa Street, Layinka Street, Cemetery Road, Bakare Faro Street, Adejiyan Street, Ishaga Street, Onishapa Street, Itire Street, Ojo Road, and Signal Barracks (end point of the race).

All junctions and intersections along the corridor from Maracana Stadium to Signal Barracks, Ojo Road, will be temporarily closed and manned by LASTMA, the Nigeria Police Force (NPF), Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), and Lagos State Neighbourhood Corps (LSNC) to restrict access during the marathon.

However, these junctions will be opened intermittently to allow controlled movement of other road users as the race progresses. Motorists are therefore advised to use the following alternative routes:

Alternative Routes
1. Traffic from Berger/Apapa–Oshodi Expressway heading to Olodi Apapa via Kirikiri should turn right into Industrial Road, link Idewu Street, proceed to Oluwa Street, connect Tolu Road, and link Baale Road to continue their journey.

2. Traffic from Suru-Alaba (Lagos–Badagry Expressway) heading to Gaskiya Road and Iganmu Road will use a contra-flow on Cemetery Road from Techn oil turning to the roundabout to continue their movement.

3. Traffic from Suru-Alaba (Lagos–Badagry Expressway) heading to Ojo Road should turn left before Signal Barracks into Charles Avenue, link Ligali Street, proceed to Evie Street, connect Abeje Street, and link Ojo Road.

The Lagos State Government assures that there will be minimal impact on traffic flow within the affected corridors.
Advisory: Motorists are urged to exercise patience and cooperate with traffic management officers, as the partial road closures are essential to ensuring a safe and successful marathon.

#LASG

S.R. 401 TRAFFIC ADVISORY FROM DEC. 12 THROUGH JAN. 2026:  The following advisory is from FDOT (Florida Department of Transportation)  Motorists are advised that a continuous closure will be implemented on the State Road (S.R. 401) western movable bridge from southbound S.R. 401 to westbound S.R. 528 beginning Friday, Dec. 12. The closure is expected to remain in place through January 2026.

Southbound S.R. 401 traffic wishing to travel to westbound S.R. 528 will be directed to the middle bridge on S.R. 401 and use the access road on the west side of S.R. 401 to exit to Westbound S.R. 528 Ramp.

The closure is necessary for the rehabilitation of the movable bridge, including replacing its protective paint layers and mechanical equipment. The other two bridges will remain open to accommodate both northbound and southbound traffic. Marine traffic may cause the bridges to close temporarily.

The work schedule is subject to change due to inclement weather or other unforeseen circumstances. For more details, please visit https://t.co/XPH21I1s5r

FDOT encourages motorists to use caution, remain alert, and follow posted detour signs through the work zone.
